title: Tencent releases Hy4 with safety limits on cyber and biology training data
subtitle: The Chinese tech giant says Hy4 was trained on a narrowed slice of cybersecurity and biology material to reduce misuse risk — with open weights promised in the coming days.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Tencent launched its new frontier model, Hy4, on November 4 and framed the release around safety. The company says Hy4's training data on cybersecurity was limited to defensive material and that offensive content — tutorials on building hacking tools or exploiting systems — was excluded. Tencent also says its internal security evaluators found no sign that Hy4 raised the ceiling for helping users break into software. Weights and a safety testing report will follow in the coming days, which means outside researchers cannot yet verify any of these claims.

On biology, Tencent's internal tests report that Hy4 did not meaningfully lower the barrier to running harmful experiments. Tencent describes Hy4 as knowledgeable about biology at a textbook level but weaker than frontier Western models at designing novel open-ended experiments. Reporting from Interesting Engineering cites a 7.2% hallucination rate on Tencent's internal benchmark, which the company frames as competitive with frontier systems. As with the safety claims, treat the benchmark number as company-stated until the report is published.

The release sits inside a wider pattern. Chinese labs have been shipping capable open-weight models at a steady cadence through 2026 — Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro, Mistral Large 4, Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5, and others earlier this autumn. Hy4 is notable because its headline isn't a capability number but a deliberate choice to restrict training data. That runs against the common assumption that more training data on more topics always wins, and matches a narrower approach that labs in the US and UK AI safety institutes have been pushing privately.

Takeaway for learners: capability and safety are not opposites, but they are not the same axis either. A model that is deliberately weaker at a dangerous skill can still be excellent at everything else — and for high-stakes deployments, that tradeoff may be worth more than an extra point on a general benchmark. When Tencent's safety testing report drops, compare what they measured and what they left out; the gaps are where the real argument lives.
